why: The criterion holds for all four verifier checks. Check 1's PASS and FAIL only test that clamp is exported and limits x to the range. Getting lo below the range, hi above it, and x unchanged inside it, endpoints included, is what "limited to the range lo to hi" means. Check 2 only tests that a RangeError is thrown when lo > hi. Check 3 asks that each exported function "appears in README.md with a description of what it does". That matches "documents" and does not require a heading layout. Check 4 only tests the exit status and that no tests fail. Everything stricter is under "Advisory (does not affect PASS or FAIL)": the clamp tests in test/math.test.js, a heading per function under '## API', and lo === hi. The parenthetical "which should include add, subtract, multiply and clamp" only describes what the export list should contain. It adds no requirement beyond the words.
